style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff2f1;strokeColor=#e5534b;fontSize=11;align=center;" value="NOT pressed → pin sits at 3.3 V → reads HIGH (1)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="30" width="300" x="360" y="120" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="readdown" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#e8f5e9;strokeColor=#43a047;fontSize=11;align=center;" value="pressed → connects pin to GND → reads LOW (0)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="30" width="300" x="360" y="158" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="phys" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#eef6ff;strokeColor=#4a90d9;fontSize=12;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacing=8;" value="⚡ <b>Physics:</b> an input pin measures voltage. Left alone, a bare wire "floats" and picks up electrical noise — random 1s and 0s. The <b>pull-up resistor</b> (we turn on the ESP32's built-in one with Pin.PULL_UP) gently ties the pin to 3.3 V, so it reads a steady HIGH. Pressing the button shorts the pin straight to GND (0 V), which wins, so it reads LOW. That's why the button is <b>active-low</b>: pressed = 0. (A press bounces for a few ms, so the code "debounces" it.)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="130" width="760" x="60" y="420" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div: ⚡ Physics: an input pin measures voltage. Left alone, a bare wire "floats" and picks up electrical noise — random 1s and 0s. The pull-up resistor (we turn on the ESP32's built-in one with Pin.PULL_UP) gently ties the pin to 3.3 V, so it reads a steady HIGH. Pressing the button shorts the pin straight to GND (0 V), which wins, so it reads LOW. That's why the button is active-low: pressed = 0. (A press bounces for a few ms, so the code "debounces" it.)
